hook.text: A chocolate eaten in 30 seconds gives less pleasure than the same chocolate eaten in two minutes. Speed kills joy.

buildup.text: Fred Bryant defined savoring as the deliberate act of attending to and appreciating positive experiences.

discovery.text: Savoring extends the neurochemical response. Paying attention to joy literally makes the dopamine last longer.

twist.text: Photography can kill savoring. Studies show people who photograph sunsets enjoy them less than those who just watch.

climax.text: The richest people aren't the happiest because wealth reduces savoring. When you can have anything, nothing thrills.

punchline.text: Joy lasts as long as your attention does.

quiz.question: What did studies find about photographing positive experiences?
